decisions.reason: An evening psychiatric day-patient program fits a care provider's therapeutic portfolio and having its own page suggests a meaningful commitment despite higher staffing and regulatory complexity.

A custom-furniture carpentry workshop is comparatively far from the firm's core residential-care business and, even if it has its own page, it is more exposed to weak margins and strategic refocusing.
Outpatient sociotherapy complements residential and community-based support well, can strengthen care pathways, and is a plausible adjacent service for a German care organization.
Counseling for senior living is highly aligned with the core business, likely supports admissions and client acquisition, and its home-page visibility signals strategic importance.

A retail shop linked to a sheltered workshop is peripheral to core care services and, with only limited website emphasis, is the most likely candidate to be discontinued if management reallocates resources.
